stem.text: In a radioactive decay series, three successive decays each result in a particle being emitted.

The first decay results in the emission of a $\beta^{-}$ particle. The second decay results in the emission of an $\alpha$ particle. The third decay results in the emission of another $\beta^{-}$ particle.

stem.alt: Decay scheme with nuclides P, Q, R and S joined by arrows, with β- written above the arrow from P to Q, α above the arrow from Q to R, and β- above the arrow from R to S.

stem.text: Nuclides P and S are compared.

A.text: P and S are identical in all respects.

B.text: P and S are isotopes of the same element.

C.text: S is a different element of lower atomic number.

D.text: S is a different element of reduced mass.
